direct_claims: The chart shows global HIV/AIDS death rates per 100,000 people by age group from 1980 to 2023.
It is produced by Our World in Data using data from the IHME, Global Burden of Disease (2025).
Death rates are measured per 100,000 individuals within each specific age bracket.
derived_claims: The purpose of this visualization is to track historical progress and highlight age-specific disparities in HIV/AIDS mortality globally over more than four decades.
The peak in global death rates occurred in the late 1990s to mid-2000s across most age groups, with the 15-49 age group peaking highest at approximately 36 deaths per 100,000 in 2003.
The '<5 years old' group peaked earlier (around 1999-2000 at ~32 per 100,000) and fell dramatically, which is highly correlated with pediatric HIV prevention initiatives.
Death rates for 50-69 years old (~15 per 100,000) and 15-49 years old (~13 per 100,000) remain the highest in 2023.
The 5-14 age group consistently maintained the lowest death rate throughout the entire period, peaking at only around 3.5 per 100,000 in the mid-2000s.
speculative_claims: The sharp decline after the mid-2000s reflects the global rollout of antiretroviral therapy (ART) and mother-to-child transmission prevention programs.
The dramatic reduction in death rates across all age groups demonstrates the massive impact of global health interventions, funding (such as PEPFAR and the Global Fund), and medical advancements.
Continued funding and access to healthcare are critical to maintaining these downward trends and preventing a resurgence.
